## Mapping

```{r}
#load libraries 

#install.packages(c("maptiles","tidyterra","leaflet", "tidygeocoder", "ggspatial")) 

library(sf)
library(tidyverse) #meta-package used for cleaning data for easy workflow  
library(here) #enable easy file referencing 
library(maptiles) #downloads tile basemaps
library(tidyterra) #plot terra rasters in ggplot2
library(leaflet) #create interactive maps
library(tidygeocoder) #provides mechanisms to use free geocoding services
library(ggspatial) #provide spatial dataframework for ggplot2; includes cartographic annotations: north arrows and scale bars

```

## Chemical Data Import

```{r}
#import maunalua chemical data 
chemi <- read.csv(here("Week_04","data","chemicaldata_maunalua.csv"))

glimpse(chemi)

chemi_dd_clean <- chemi |>
  drop_na() |>
  separate_wider_delim(cols = "Tide_time",
                       delim = "_",
                       names = c("Tide", "Time"),
                       cols_remove = FALSE)

```
# Downloading Tile Basemaps 

We will use the code: {maptiles} to download satellite and street map tiles. Having internet is necessary to be able to download. Maptiles is similar to  Google maps, as in it stitches together various parts of the map to form the bigger images.

```{r}
#maptiles - figures which tiles needed > downloads them > stitches them together into one image
#define areas of interest, by setting bounding box of lat and longi = focus on Wailupe, Oahu 
# xmin /xmax = westmost /eastmost longitude
# ymin/ymax = southernmost /northernmost latitude 

#st_as_sfc() need to download library(sf) prior to this; converts this into sf() geometric object so maptiles can read 
# st_bbox () creates bounding box rectangle
# crs (coordinate system) = 4326 specifies that WGS84 (basic lat/long system on your GPS) - almost all GPS and web page data uses this coordinate system 

wailupe_bbox <- st_as_sfc(
  st_bbox(c(xmin = -157.772, ymin = 21.267,
            xmax = -157.752, ymax = 21.281),
          crs = 4326))

```

# Download Tiles

```{r}
tiles_satellite <- get_tiles( 
  wailupe_bbox, #area to download
  provider = "Esri.WorldImagery", #which tile source to use; ESRI is case sensitive
  zoom = 16, #level of detail (3 = continent & 20 = building)
  crop = TRUE, #clip to our exact bbox (vs slightly larger)
  cachedir = here("Week_07", "data", "tiles_cache")) #save raw image tiles once to disk 

```

```{r}
#what does get_tiles return?
# spatraster - raster image (grid if pixels) from terra package
# raster - matrix of pixel values 
# tiles_satellite has 3 layers (red, green, blue) 
# cannot use geom_raster() bc that expects a dataframe not a terra object 

class(tiles_satellite)


#tidyterra bridges gap with geo_spatraster

```

```{r}
#geom_spatraster_rgb is from tidyterra. 
#Reads the 3 color layers and renders them as a photo

ggplot() + 
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = tiles_satellite) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) + #always include coordinates in WGS84. Include it in plotting spatial data - ensure map isnt distorted and that scale bars work correctly later. 
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
tiles_street <- get_tiles( 
  wailupe_bbox, #area to download
  provider = "CartoDB.Positron", #which tile source to use; ESRI is case sensitive
  zoom = 16, #level of detail (3 = continent & 20 = building)
  crop = TRUE, #clip to our exact bbox (vs slightly larger)
  cachedir = here("Week_07", "data", "tiles_cache")) #save raw image tiles once to disk 

ggplot() + 
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = tiles_street) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) + 
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
# Step 1: convert your data frame to an sf object
# coords tells sf which columns hold longitude and latitude
chemi_sf <- st_as_sf(chemi_dd_clean,
                         coords = c("Long", "Lat"),
                         crs = 4326)

# Step 2: get the bounding box and add a small buffer
# the + c(...) pads all four sides by ~0.4 km so points aren't at the edge
bbox_chem <- st_bbox(chemi_sf) + c(-0.004, -0.004, 0.004, 0.004)

# Step 3: download tiles for that extent
Map_satellite <- get_tiles(
  st_as_sfc(bbox_chem),
  provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
  zoom = 15,
  crop = TRUE,
  cachedir = here("Week_07", "data", "tiles_cache")
)
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = Map_satellite) +
  geom_point(data = chemi_dd_clean,
             aes(x = Long, y = Lat,
                 color = Salinity),
             size = 4) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = Map_satellite) +
  geom_point(data = chemi_dd_clean,
             aes(x = Long, y = Lat,
                 color = Salinity),
             size = 4) +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  annotation_scale(           # scale bar
    location = "bl",          # bl = bottom-left
    bar_cols = c("yellow", "white")) +
  annotation_north_arrow(     # north arrow
    location = "tl") +        # tl = top-left
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = Map_satellite) +
  geom_point(data = chemi_dd_clean,
             aes(x = Long, y = Lat, color = Salinity),
             size = 4) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Salinity (ppt)") +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl",
                   bar_cols = c("yellow", "white")) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl") +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
  labs(title = "Maunalua Bay — Water Chemistry",
       caption = "Basemap: ESRI World Imagery") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(here("Week_07", "output", "maunalua_map.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r}
#leaflet() |>                       # 1. create the map widget
#  addProviderTiles(...) |>         # 2. add a basemap tile layer
# addCircleMarkers(...) |>         # 3. add your data as markers
# addLegend(...)                   # 4. add a color legend


leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  setView(lng = -157.762, lat = 21.274, zoom = 14)
```
```{r}
my_map <- leaflet(data = chemi_dd_clean)
my_map<- addProviderTiles(my_map,"Esri.WorldImagery")

pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis", domain = chemi_dd_clean$Salinity)

my_map_1 <- addCircleMarkers(
  map = my_map,
  lng = ~Long,
  lat = ~Lat,
  color = ~pal(Salinity))
```

```{r}
# colorNumeric() returns a FUNCTION, not a color vector
pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis",            # any RColorBrewer or viridis palette name
  domain = chemi_dd_clean$Salinity      # the full range of values to map
)

# Use it by calling pal(value) — it returns a hex color
pal(30)  # what color does salinity = 30 get?


pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = chemi_dd_clean$Salinity)

leaflet(chemi_dd_clean) |>           # pass data frame here
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~Long, lat = ~Lat,   # which columns are coordinates
    color = ~pal(Salinity),    # apply our color function to Salinity
    radius = 6,
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~paste("Salinity:", Salinity, "ppt",  # click a point to see this
                   "<br>Site:", Site)) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = pal,                 # the same color function
    values = ~Salinity,        # which column drives the legend
    title = "Salinity (ppt)",
    position = "bottomright")
```

```{r}
oahu_sites <- tribble(
  ~place,
  "University of Hawaii at Manoa",
  "Honolulu International Airport",
  "Pearl Harbor National Memorial, Hawaii",
  "Diamond Head State Monument, Hawaii"
)

oahu_geocoded <- oahu_sites |>
  geocode(place, method = "osm") # geocode the 'place' column

oahu_geocoded
```
```{r}
leaflet(oahu_geocoded) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~long, lat = ~lat,   # tidygeocoder always returns 'lat' and 'long'
    label = ~place)            # hover to see place name
```
